evaluated.name: CashSalesToPrice
evaluated.expression: RATIO(ADD(sale, ADD(recch, invch)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
evaluated.hypothesis: Sales-to-price is a strong value signal only when revenue converts into cash; adjusting sales for receivable and inventory build-ups (cash-flow-statement decrease items, negative when working capital expands) yields a cash sales yield that avoids revenue-recognition-driven value traps.
evaluated.reasoning: Operating-cycle accruals are the specific accrual channel that contaminates revenue-based valuation, so correcting the numerator of the sales multiple targets the mechanism directly rather than adding a generic accrual score. It tests a different valuation anchor (revenue) and a different accrual primitive (working-capital cash-flow items) than Signals 1–3.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: OpaqueValueAccrualInstability
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cheapness is only investable when the accounting is legible: firms with volatile, unstable accruals are informationally opaque, so their low multiples reflect justified uncertainty, while cheap firms with stable accrual behavior are genuinely mispriced.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the level of accruals with the second moment of accruals, a distinct information-risk mechanism rather than an earnings-overstatement mechanism, gated onto an EBITDA-based cheapness measure that is itself pre-accrual. If it outperforms Signal 1, the interaction is about accounting reliability rather than accrual direction.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ConjunctiveValueAccrualScreen
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cheapness and accrual conservatism are complements, not substitutes: the value premium is earned only when a firm passes both screens, so the expected return is governed by the weaker of the two percentile scores rather than by their average.
evaluated.reasoning: Working in bounded industry-rank space removes the negative-book-equity perversity of the multiplicative gate, since a good accrual rank can no longer push a distressed firm further into the short leg. The MIN aggregation is a substantively different claim from the published additive value-plus-accruals composite: it predicts no premium for accrual-clean expensive firms or for accrual-heavy cheap firms, which a linear blend rewards partially.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AccrualRegimeReversalValue
evaluated.expression: SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cheap firms whose current accruals sit at the low end of their own five-year accrual history have already absorbed the reversal of past aggressive reporting; the market extrapolates the recent weak reported earnings, so the discount is stale and mean-reverts upward.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the flawed "purged equity" arithmetic entirely, so no depreciation add-back can inflate the valuation anchor: depreciation enters only inside a self-referenced time-series rank, where firm-level capital intensity is differenced away. The mechanism is a within-firm accrual regime state (reversal completed) interacted with cross-sectional cheapness, which is distinct from any accrual-level composite.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: HardBookToMarket
evaluated.expression: RATIO(SUB(ceq, SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
evaluated.hypothesis: Book equity composed of receivables, inventories and other soft operating working capital is far less reliable collateral for a value claim than equity composed of cash and long-lived assets; restating the value anchor on hard, non-accrual equity identifies cheapness that is not an artifact of accrual-inflated current assets.
evaluated.reasoning: This is not operating cash flow to price, because it uses the stock of net operating working capital rather than its change, so it cannot collapse to the documented CF/P anomaly and it prices the accumulated accrual balance that reversal risk actually lives on. Firms whose book equity is mostly working capital receive a sharply lower signal even at identical B/M, which is exactly the value-trap distinction the theme calls for.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: OpaqueOtherAccrualValue
evaluated.expression: SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(ABS(RATIO(aoloch, at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Large "other" operating asset and liability adjustments are the least verifiable accrual component and proxy for accounting opacity; cheapness is credible when the cash-flow reconciliation is dominated by transparent items, and is a trap when a big unexplained residual accrual drives reported operations.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the published glamour-conditioned accrual result with an untested opacity channel on the value side, and taking absolute magnitude makes the quality leg sign-unambiguous (both large positive and large negative residual accruals indicate unverifiable reporting). Because both legs are industry ranks, the long leg is cheap-and-transparent and the short leg is expensive-and-opaque, avoiding the perverse mixed long leg of the earlier multiplicative form.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashEbitdaToEnterpriseValue
evaluated.expression: RATIO(SUB(ebitda, DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Operating profit that must be reinvested in receivables and inventories is not distributable to capital providers; measuring cheapness as working-capital-adjusted EBITDA per dollar of enterprise value identifies firms whose whole-capital-structure multiple is supported by cash-convertible profit rather than by working-capital-inflated accounting profit.
evaluated.reasoning: The enterprise-value denominator prices debt and net cash, making this a different valuation anchor from book-to-market and hence less collinear with HML, while the numerator subtracts the exact accrual component that makes EBITDA unreliable. It tests whether moving the interaction into an EV multiple recovers the FF5 alpha that equity-only value anchors failed to deliver.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: SoftCapitalBackedPriceTrap
evaluated.expression: RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
evaluated.hypothesis: What matters for a value trap is not the annual accrual flow but the accumulated stock of soft operating capital standing behind the price: when a large share of market value is claimed by receivables and inventories net of operating liabilities, the equity claim rests on assets whose realization is uncertain and whose write-down is pending, so such firms underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the flow-over-market-cap deflator (a known accrual-anomaly robustness variant) with the balance-sheet accrual *stock* per dollar of price, a quantity that is not the accrual anomaly variable and that decomposes book-to-market into its hard and soft halves. Paired with the archived HardBookToMarket it delivers a clean decomposition test: if the hard half carries the positive slope and the soft half a negative one, the value premium is genuinely accrual-quality conditional rather than uniform.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CheapnessWeightedAccrualQuality
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accrual conservatism is priced only where the market has already assigned a low multiple, so the correct signal is accrual quality amplified by the firm's cheapness percentile: among expensive firms the accrual term is muted, among cheap firms it fully separates cash-backed value from accrual-supported value traps.
evaluated.reasoning: Unlike the symmetric z-score product, one leg is a bounded [0,1] cheapness weight and only the accrual leg is signed, so the long and short extremes are both drawn from cheap firms (clean versus dirty) instead of pooling cheap-clean with expensive-dirty. That construction also makes the spread approximately value-neutral, which directly targets the gen-1 failure in which static-value loadings caused FF5 to absorb or over-price the entire raw spread.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashFundedExpansionValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUB(RATIO(DELTA(che, 1), at), RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: For a cheap firm the informative question is what its balance sheet grew into: cash accumulation means reported profits were collected, while growth concentrated in receivables and inventories means profits exist only on paper, so the cash-versus-soft-capital composition of expansion discriminates real from illusory cheapness.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the flawed price-driven "value news" leg — which was mechanically past return and thus a reversal bet — with a purely fundamental composition measure that contains no price change at all. Because the cheapness term enters as a bounded weight, the long-short spread again compares cheap firms with cheap firms, so the mechanism is testable without an embedded HML position.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CurrentLiabilityStretchedValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(DELTA(lct, 1), MA(sale, 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cheap firms that expand payables and accrued liabilities faster than their normalized revenue are financing operations by stretching suppliers and deferring recognized costs, which simultaneously flatters operating cash flow and raises refinancing risk, so their low multiple reflects a deteriorating rather than a temporarily depressed business.
evaluated.reasoning: This tests the liability side of the accrual construct, a channel none of the archived signals touches, and normalizing by three-year average sales avoids the scale artifacts of asset deflation for firms with shrinking balance sheets. Because it explicitly predicts a negative slope within the cheap cohort, it also serves as the sign-symmetric counterpart to Signal 2: both should be strong if the trap mechanism is real, and their disagreement would localize whether asset-side or liability-side accruals drive the effect.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: WorstFlawPenalizedValue
evaluated.expression: SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MAX(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at), 1)), IND_RANK(ABS(RATIO(aoloch, at)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accounting credibility is destroyed by whichever red flag is worst, not by their average: a cheap firm is a trap if either its working-capital accruals are large or its cash-flow reconciliation is dominated by unexplained other-accrual items, so cheapness should be penalized by the maximum of the two flaw percentiles.
evaluated.reasoning: The MAX operates on the accrual side rather than across themes, which is a different aggregation claim from the archived MIN screen: it lets two economically distinct accounting flaws substitute for each other as disqualifiers while keeping a single continuous value ladder. Winsorizing the accrual leg and using absolute opacity keeps both flaw measures sign-unambiguous and bounded, and comparing this to the archived single-flaw versions tells us whether accrual red flags are additive or worst-case in their pricing effect.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashShareOfCurrentAssetsValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(che, act)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The stock analogue of the winning flow signal: among cheap firms, those whose current assets are held as cash rather than as receivables and inventories have already collected their reported profits, whereas cheap firms whose liquidity is locked in soft claims face reversal and write-down risk.
evaluated.reasoning: CashFundedExpansionValue showed that the cash-versus-soft-capital composition of the balance sheet, weighted by cheapness, produces FF5 alpha; this tests whether the effect lives in the level of composition or only in its annual change, which is the single most useful thing to learn about that mechanism. The ratio is bounded in [0,1] by construction, so the accrual leg needs no winsorization and the long-short legs are both drawn from cheap firms, keeping the spread near value-neutral.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: SoftCapitalPerEnterpriseValue
evaluated.expression: RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The value trap is that total invested capital, not just equity, is committed to soft operating claims: when receivables and inventories net of operating liabilities consume a large share of enterprise value, both shareholders and creditors are exposed to accrual reversal, and expected returns are lower than the firm's factor loadings imply.
evaluated.reasoning: This isolates the deflator choice in the archive's strongest portfolio result, replacing market equity with enterprise value so that the signal is no longer mechanically inflated by leverage and thin equity capitalization. If the negative alpha survives the debt-inclusive deflator, the trap is about the composition of invested capital rather than about a levered small-cap value tilt.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: WorkingCapitalTurnoverValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(sale, SUB(act, che))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accrual assets are only dangerous when they are unproductive: a cheap firm that turns each dollar of receivables and inventory into many dollars of revenue is converting accruals into realized sales quickly, while a cheap firm with slow working-capital turnover is warehousing claims that will be written down.
evaluated.reasoning: This introduces a new channel — the velocity of accrual assets rather than their level, change, or composition — while keeping the cheapness-weight structure that produced the archive's only positive alpha. Turnover is a strictly positive, well-scaled quantity with broad coverage, and industry z-scoring removes the large sector differences in normal operating-cycle length.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: WorkedDownWorkingCapitalValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), at), 5), RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A cheap firm that has already worked its receivable and inventory bloat well below its own five-year peak has completed the accrual reversal the market feared, so its discount is stale; a cheap firm still sitting at its historical working-capital peak has the reversal, and the associated write-downs, still ahead of it.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a distance-from-own-extreme state rather than a level, a one-year change, or a cumulative flow, so it is not a horizon reparameterization of CashFundedExpansionValue: two firms with identical current accruals and identical annual changes receive opposite scores depending on where they stand relative to their own historical bloat. Keeping the cheapness term as a bounded weight preserves the near value-neutral long-short structure that produced the archive's only positive alpha, while the five-year window supplies the reversal-completion concept the mechanism requires.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: DebtFinancedSoftCapitalTrap
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), MA(at, 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Soft operating capital is most dangerous when it is financed by creditors rather than by equity: a levered firm whose market value is largely backed by receivables and inventories faces creditor-forced liquidation of exactly those claims at distressed prices, so the combination of high soft-capital-per-price and high leverage predicts returns below factor loadings.
evaluated.reasoning: This keeps the archive's strongest portfolio mechanism (soft capital per dollar of price, alpha −4.5%/yr, t = −4.0) and adds the economically motivated amplifier the earlier EV proposal was trying and failing to express, but the leverage conditioner is a ratio of strictly positive quantities, so no negative or near-zero enterprise-value denominators can invert the ordering. It also converts the leverage idea into a genuine interaction claim — the trap intensity depends on who funds the accrual assets — rather than a valuation-anchor swap.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AccrualNonArticulationValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(ABS(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), NEG(ADD(recch, ADD(invch, apalch))))), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: When the balance-sheet change in working capital does not reconcile with the working-capital items reported in the cash-flow statement, the gap reflects acquisitions, reclassifications, write-offs and other discretion that makes the accounting hard to audit; cheapness is credible when the two accrual measurements articulate and is a trap when they diverge.
evaluated.reasoning: The discriminating variable is neither the level nor the direction of accruals but the internal consistency of two independent measurements of the same accrual — a measurement-integrity channel the archive has never tested, and one that is zero for a clean, organically operating firm regardless of how large its accruals are. Winsorizing and asset-scaling the discrepancy keeps it bounded, and pairing it with the bounded cheapness weight retains the value-neutral spread structure, at the cost of the narrower coverage of the cash-flow-statement working-capital items.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: TurnoverImprovementValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(sale, SUB(act, che)), 1), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: A cheap firm whose working-capital turnover is accelerating is liquidating accrual assets into realized sales and thereby validating its depressed multiple, whereas slowing turnover at a low multiple signals inventory and receivables accumulating faster than the business can convert them.
evaluated.reasoning: Paired with Signal 1 this decomposes the velocity channel into a structural level and a directional change, which is the key unresolved design question for the archive's best joint result. Unlike the earlier flagged change signals, no price term enters the change leg, so it cannot degenerate into a past-return reversal bet.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: NetLiquidBackingToPrice
evaluated.expression: RATIO(SUB(che, SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
evaluated.hypothesis: What the market pays for should be judged by the hardness of the claims behind it: cash net of soft operating working capital measures the genuinely liquid backing per dollar of price, and firms whose price is supported by cash rather than by unrealized receivable and inventory claims earn higher subsequent returns.
evaluated.reasoning: The two largest alphas in the archive are the cash-share signal (+5.5%) and the soft-capital-per-price trap (−3.7%), which are opposite ends of the same composition idea; netting them into a single price-scaled ratio tests whether they are one effect and, unlike the rank-weighted forms, produces a signed cross-sectional variable that the Fama-MacBeth regression can price directly. This is the design most likely to align the FMB slope with the portfolio evidence rather than leaving them in conflict.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: OperatingCycleInstabilityValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(VOL(RATIO(sale, SUB(act, che)), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cheapness is credible when the operating cycle is predictable: a firm whose working-capital turnover swings erratically has accrual assets whose realizable value is unknowable to outsiders, so its discount reflects genuine information risk rather than mispricing.
evaluated.reasoning: This adds the second moment of the velocity channel, distinguishing "fast" from "reliable" conversion, and it revisits the instability idea that failed in gen 1 with an EBITDA-yield anchor and a Sloan-flow volatility measure — now applied to the operating-cycle variable that actually generates alpha. If stability dominates level, refinement should move toward predictability metrics; if not, the channel is purely about speed.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: SupplierFundedCycleValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), SUB(act, che)), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: A cheap firm whose operating cycle is funded by suppliers and accrued expenses rather than by its own capital needs no cash to grow and collects before it pays, so a high ratio of operating liabilities to operating current assets marks cheapness backed by structural cash generation rather than by working-capital investment.
evaluated.reasoning: This reframes the liability side as a financing advantage rather than the "stretching" distress story that produced a strong FMB slope but no alpha in gen 2, and it is a composition ratio rather than a change, so it is not the sign-flipped Sloan accrual the critic rejected. It also completes the accrual-composition map: asset softness (tested), asset velocity (tested), and now who finances the assets.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: DepreciationConservatismValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dp, MA(at, 3)), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Long-lived asset accounting, not just working capital, determines whether cheapness is real: a firm that charges heavy depreciation relative to its normalized asset base is writing its assets down aggressively, so its book equity and reported earnings are understated and its low multiple overstates how expensive it truly is, while a cheap firm with unusually light depreciation is carrying stale asset values that will eventually be impaired.
evaluated.reasoning: This moves the accrual leg from the working-capital cycle — the only accrual channel the archive has explored — to the depreciation channel, which is the second large non-cash component of earnings and is entirely untested here, so the result is informative regardless of sign. Industry z-scoring strips out sector capital intensity so the surviving variation is within-industry accounting conservatism, and three-year average assets in the denominator avoids the mechanical spike that a shrinking asset base would create.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: VelocityScreenedValue
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(sale, SUB(act, che)), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cheapness and operating-asset velocity are complements that must both be present: a firm qualifies as cash-verified value only if it is cheap *and* converts its receivables and inventories into revenue quickly, so expected return is governed by the weaker of the two percentile scores rather than by a soft product of a weight and a score.
evaluated.reasoning: This isolates one specific design choice — hard weakest-link screening versus the soft rank-times-z-score weighting — on the only mechanism in the archive that is significant on both the cross-sectional and portfolio dimensions, and MIN-of-ranks was previously the structure that produced the archive's strongest FMB slope (4.36). Because both legs are bounded industry ranks with no shared denominator, the construction avoids the mechanical linkage that made the cash-share plus velocity rank-sum uninterpretable, and the hard screen should tighten the extreme deciles that currently generate conflicting FMB and alpha evidence.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: TurnoverLevelAndImprovementValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(WINSOR(RATIO(sale, SUB(act, che)), 1), WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(sale, SUB(act, che)), 1), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cheapness is most credible when accrual assets are both structurally fast-turning and currently accelerating: the level tells us the firm has a short cash cycle, the change tells us the cycle is not silently lengthening, and a cheap firm satisfying both is converting reported claims into realized revenue.
evaluated.reasoning: The two legs are the archive's only constructions strong on FMB, alpha, and Sharpe simultaneously, and unlike the rejected cash-share plus turnover pairing they are not mechanically linked through a shared denominator — one is a cross-sectional level, the other its own first difference. Winsorizing before ranking repairs the outlier defect the critic identified in both parents, so this is the natural consolidation test of the velocity channel.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitVelocityValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ebitda, SUB(act, che)), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: What matters is not how much revenue passes through accrual assets but how much cash profit they generate: a cheap firm earning high operating profit per dollar of receivables and inventory has working capital that is genuinely productive, whereas high revenue throughput at zero margin means the accrual assets are being churned without creating value.
evaluated.reasoning: This isolates whether the velocity channel works through throughput (sales) or through profit conversion (EBITDA) on the identical accrual-asset base, which distinguishes a DuPont-style turnover effect from a genuine cash-generation effect and tells us which quantity to build on in the final generations. It keeps the value weight and winsorization design that has produced joint evidence, changing only the numerator of the quality leg.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ExcessLiquidBackingOverValue
evaluated.expression: SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(che, SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The informative quantity is how much *more* liquid the backing of a firm's price is than its overall book cheapness would imply: a firm ranked far higher on cash-net-of-soft-working-capital per dollar of price than on book-to-market has hard, immediately realizable value the market is ignoring, while the reverse ordering marks a firm whose book cheapness is entirely soft claims.
evaluated.reasoning: The liquidity-composition cluster generated the archive's largest alphas but near-zero raw Sharpe, the signature of a spread that is a levered value tilt hedged by FF5; differencing the two industry ranks removes the common book-to-market component so both legs of the portfolio contain similarly cheap firms and the surviving variation is purely balance-sheet hardness. This is the most direct available test of whether that cluster contains a tradable effect or only a factor-loading artifact.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: TaxCorroboratedValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(txp, MA(sale, 3)), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Tax authorities are an independent auditor of reported profit: a cheap firm carrying substantial current income taxes payable relative to its normalized revenue is earning income that the tax system also recognizes, whereas a cheap firm reporting profits with negligible tax obligations is generating book income that no external party has validated.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the working-capital-velocity family entirely and tests the book-tax corroboration channel, which the archive has never touched despite taxes payable being one of the accrual-theme primitives. Normalizing by three-year average revenue rather than income avoids the near-zero-denominator explosion that a percent-of-earnings scaling would create, and industry z-scoring removes the large sectoral differences in effective tax exposure.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: VelocityAndDepreciationQualityValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(WINSOR(RATIO(sale, SUB(act, che)), 1), WINSOR(RATIO(dp, MA(at, 3)), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accounting quality has two independent dimensions for a cheap firm — how quickly its short-term accrual assets convert into revenue, and how conservatively it writes down its long-lived assets — and cheapness supported on both dimensions is least likely to be a value trap.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the mechanically correlated pairing the critic rejected: the two legs live in different regions of the balance sheet, so a firm with low operating working capital gains no automatic advantage on the depreciation leg. Both parents also had correctly signed FMB slopes (velocity 3.91, depreciation conservatism 2.86), so unlike the reversal-completion leg with its −1.68 slope, the composite has a coherent chance of joint cross-sectional and portfolio strength.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: BuybackVerifiedCheapness
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), MA(sale, 3)), 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cash returned by retiring shares is the hardest possible verification that a cheap firm's reported profits were actually collected, and it is credible only if the operating cycle was not simultaneously absorbing cash; a cheap firm shrinking its share count while releasing working capital is distributing real cash, whereas one issuing shares while building receivables and inventories is funding uncollected profit with equity.
evaluated.reasoning: This implements the payout-verification hypothesis with a continuously distributed financing variable rather than dividends, eliminating both the zero-payer mass point and the scale domination that made the previous expression collapse into the working-capital accrual leg. Combining the two legs in rank space guarantees each contributes equally by construction, so the signal genuinely tests financing-side cash return jointly with operating-side cash release.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: VelocityAndBuybackValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(sale, SUB(act, che)), 1), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The two strongest independent confirmations that a cheap firm's earnings are real are that it is retiring shares with cash and that its accrual assets are converting into revenue faster than before; a firm doing both is returning cash it has actually collected.
evaluated.reasoning: This pairs the archive's best Sharpe leg (share retirement, from BuybackVerifiedCheapness) with its best FMB leg (turnover improvement, fmb 3.62 with Sharpe 0.339), two channels drawn from different financial statements with no shared denominator, so the complementarity claim is clean unlike the earlier rejected pairings. If it beats both parents on ls_talpha and Sharpe, the final generations should build on financing-plus-velocity rather than financing-plus-accrual-level.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: TripleVerifiedCheapness
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), SUMRANK(WINSOR(RATIO(sale, SUB(act, che)), 1), NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), MA(sale, 3)), 1))))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cheapness backed by three independent accounting confirmations — cash returned through share retirement, a structurally fast operating cycle, and working capital that is being released rather than absorbed — is the least likely to be a value trap, and the confirmations should aggregate rather than substitute.
evaluated.reasoning: This is the full consolidation of the three legs that have each produced correctly signed evidence, aggregated in bounded rank space so no leg dominates by scale. Its comparison against Signals 1 and 2 tells us whether accounting verification is genuinely multi-dimensional or whether one channel (financing discipline) subsumes the operating channels, which is the central question to answer before the final generations.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: HardBookAnchoredVerifiedValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), MA(sale, 3)), 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The conditioning variable should itself be accrual-purged: measuring cheapness against book equity net of soft operating working capital ranks firms by hard-asset value per dollar of price, so the cash-verification legs are applied to a cleaner definition of who is genuinely cheap.
evaluated.reasoning: Every strong signal in the archive has used raw book-to-market as its weight, and HardBookToMarket was independently correctly signed (fmb 2.29), so upgrading the anchor while holding the winning quality composite fixed isolates the value-side design choice that has never been tested inside the successful architecture. If the alpha and Sharpe improve, the final signal should carry a purged anchor.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: DeleveragingVerifiedValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), MA(sale, 3)), 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: If the buyback result reflects genuine cash generation rather than an equity-issuance anomaly, then debt repayment should work the same way: a cheap firm paying down borrowings while releasing working capital is servicing claims with collected cash, whereas one borrowing to fund receivables and inventories is financing uncollected profit.
evaluated.reasoning: This is the decisive economic test of what drives the archive's leading signal — cash verification, as hypothesized, or the published net-share-issuance effect — because it swaps the financing instrument while holding the operating leg and structure identical. A comparable result would establish the general mechanism; a null would tell the final generations that the equity-retirement channel is doing the work and should be kept explicit.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: OwnHistoryCheapnessVerifiedValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), MA(sale, 3)), 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What makes a value trap is not being cheap relative to other firms but being cheap relative to what this business has historically been worth; a firm trading at the top of its own five-year book-to-market range while retiring shares and releasing working capital is being discounted despite verified cash generation, and that discount should revert.
evaluated.reasoning: This changes the valuation side from a cross-sectional to a within-firm benchmark, a concept the archive has never tested on the value leg, and it does so for a specific portfolio reason: every cross-sectionally value-weighted construction here carries an HML/CMA loading that FF5 prices away, whereas an own-history cheapness weight is close to value-factor neutral and can only earn alpha through the verification channel. It keeps the winning verification composite intact so the comparison against BuybackVerifiedCheapness isolates the anchor concept rather than a parameter.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: DualAnchorVerifiedValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), MA(sale, 3)), 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A single valuation ratio is a noisy measure of cheapness — book equity is distorted by write-offs and intangibles, revenue by margin structure — so a firm that is cheap on both an asset anchor and a revenue anchor is more reliably underpriced, and applying cash verification to that better-measured cheapness should sharpen the interaction.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the discredited third MIN-screen experiment with a measurement-error fix on the conditioning variable: agreement between two economically independent value anchors reduces the chance that the weight is picking up accounting distortion rather than genuine cheapness. It is complementary to, not overlapping with, HardBookAnchoredVerifiedValue, which purges the single anchor rather than diversifying across anchors, so the two together identify whether the value leg should be cleaned or broadened.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashAndBuybackVerifiedValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), SUB(RATIO(DELTA(che, 1), MA(at, 3)), RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), MA(at, 3))))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cash verification of cheapness has a balance-sheet signature and a financing signature: the balance-sheet signature is that expansion shows up as cash rather than as receivables and inventories, and the financing signature is that shares are being retired; a cheap firm exhibiting both has collected its reported profits and is returning them.
evaluated.reasoning: The operating leg here is the full cash-versus-soft-capital composition that produced an independent positive alpha (+2.0%, t=2.17), which is strictly more informative than the working-capital-release half used by the current leader because it also credits firms that convert profits into cash balances. Both legs remain in bounded rank space and neither depends on velocity, so the test isolates whether adding the cash-accumulation side strengthens the archive's best signal.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: TotalPayoutVerifiedValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), RATIO(dvc, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), MA(sale, 3)), 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Buybacks and dividends are substitutable forms of the same evidence — cash actually leaving the firm — so total shareholder distribution is a stronger verification of a cheap firm's earnings than share retirement alone, provided the operating cycle is not simultaneously consuming that cash.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive has never tested dividends inside a working construction; the earlier attempt failed because dvc was placed in a linear ratio where it was dominated by the working-capital term, whereas here it enters through its own rank so scale differences are irrelevant and the zero-payer mass merely occupies the bottom of one of three channels. If total payout beats buyback alone, the mechanism is cash distribution generally rather than the published net-issuance effect.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: VerificationWeightedCheapness
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), MA(sale, 3)), 1)))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The interaction can be read in either direction — a value premium that exists only among firms with verified accounting, or a quality premium that exists only among cheap firms — and the correct reading determines which variable should be the signed discriminator and which the bounded gate.
evaluated.reasoning: Every strong signal in the archive gates on value and lets accounting quality do the signing, which makes the spread nearly value-neutral and is plausibly why FF5 does not absorb it; this proposal reverses the roles so the extremes are high- and low-B/M firms drawn from the well-verified population. Comparing the two tells us whether the alpha comes from ranking value stocks by verification or from ranking verified stocks by value — an economically substantive question the archive cannot currently answer.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: SelfFundedGrowthValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), SUMRANK(WINSOR(GROWTH(sale, 1), 1), NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), MA(sale, 3)), 1))))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The strongest refutation of the value-trap interpretation is a cheap firm that is growing revenue while simultaneously releasing working capital and retiring shares — growth funded internally out of collected cash rather than out of accrual buildup or external issuance.
evaluated.reasoning: Revenue growth has never entered the archive as a channel, and it is the economically necessary complement to the working-capital leg: releasing working capital while the business shrinks is liquidation, whereas releasing it while revenue expands is genuine operating efficiency, so the two legs jointly identify a state that neither identifies alone. All three legs enter through ranks, so the growth term cannot dominate by scale and the conjunction is monotone in each channel.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: StaleWorkingCapitalTrap
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), MA(sale, 3)), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(GROWTH(sale, 1), 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The genuine value trap is the conjunction of accrual buildup and deteriorating demand: a cheap firm accumulating receivables and inventories while revenue declines is holding claims and goods that will be written down, and such firms subsequently underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: Replacing the signed product with a MIN of two bounded percentile ranks fixes the sign inconsistency the critic identified: the term is now large only when working capital is building *and* sales are falling, and the benign "release plus growth" state maps to the opposite end instead of the same end. Multiplying by the cheapness rank concentrates the diagnosis in the value cohort where trap risk is economically relevant, and the informative extreme is the short leg, which is a homogeneous group of cheap, accrual-bloating, shrinking firms.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: LongTermAccrualVerifiedValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(at, act), 1), MA(sale, 3)), 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Earnings can be inflated by capitalizing costs into long-lived assets just as easily as by building receivables, so a cheap firm whose non-current operating asset base is expanding faster than its revenue is deferring expenses onto the balance sheet, while one holding non-current assets flat relative to sales while retiring shares has earnings that are genuinely collected.
evaluated.reasoning: Every accrual leg tested so far has been confined to the working-capital cycle, yet the long-term operating accrual is the larger component of total accruals for capital-intensive firms and carries its own documented mispricing, so this extends the mechanism to a new region of the balance sheet rather than recombining tested elements. Deflating by three-year average sales keeps the interpretation as capitalization intensity relative to business volume, and coverage is as broad as the leading signals since it needs only total and current assets.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: PersistentReleaseVerifiedValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(NEG(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), 0), 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Whether working capital was released is more reliable evidence than how much was released, because magnitudes are dominated by one-off inventory writedowns and acquisitions; counting how many of the last three years showed a release identifies firms with a habitual discipline of collecting before they report.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the magnitude of the operating leg with a persistence count, a genuinely different statistic that is immune to the outliers that force winsorization and that measures a behavioural state rather than a single-year flow. Because the count takes only four values it also introduces deliberate coarseness, which should reduce portfolio turnover and, if the effect is real, raise the Sharpe of the spread relative to the magnitude-based parents.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: TrapFreeVerifiedValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), NEG(MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), MA(sale, 3)), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(GROWTH(sale, 1), 1))))))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The specific state that destroys a value thesis is accrual buildup alongside falling revenue, so the correct quality discriminator is the *absence* of that conjunction, combined with evidence of cash being returned through share retirement.
evaluated.reasoning: The gen-7 trap signal delivered the right portfolio evidence (alpha −2.2%, t = −2.61) but a wrong-signed FMB slope, because multiplying a conjunctive red flag by the cheapness rank leaves the signal positively correlated with cheapness itself; embedding the negated red flag as one leg of the standard verification composite restores sign coherence between the two evaluation dimensions. It also converts a short-only diagnostic into a long-short signal built in the architecture that has repeatedly produced joint evidence.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: QualityMarkedBookToMarket
evaluated.expression: RATIO(SUB(ceq, MUL(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(sale, SUB(act, che)))))), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
evaluated.hypothesis: Soft operating capital should be marked down in proportion to how slowly it turns rather than either counted at full book value or eliminated entirely: receivables and inventories that cycle rapidly are nearly cash, while those that sit are close to worthless, so the correct value anchor writes working capital down by its own illiquidity percentile.
evaluated.reasoning: This puts the accrual information inside the valuation ratio as a continuous haircut, which is a different construction from both raw book-to-market and the archive's HardBookToMarket that subtracts the entire working-capital balance regardless of its quality. It is also the first proposal here in which the interaction is intrinsic to the measurement of value rather than implemented as a gate times a quality score, so it tests whether the effect survives outside the winning architecture.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ConservativeEarningsYield
evaluated.expression: RATIO(MIN(ib, SUB(ib, SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp))), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
evaluated.hypothesis: A prudent investor prices a firm on the lower of its reported and its cash earnings, so positive accruals should be penalized while negative accruals earn no credit; the resulting asymmetric earnings yield identifies cheapness that holds up under the more conservative of two accounting measurements.
evaluated.reasoning: This is not the cash-flow-to-price ratio the critic rejected earlier, because MIN makes the accrual adjustment one-sided: firms whose cash flow exceeds income are valued on income, while firms whose income exceeds cash flow are valued on cash, so the numerator is a conservatism floor rather than a linear combination. The asymmetry is the economic content — accrual overstatement is punished, accrual understatement is not rewarded — and it can be tested only through a construction the archive has never used.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: LiquidationAnchoredVerifiedValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, lct), dltt), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), MA(sale, 3)), 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Net-current-asset value per dollar of price is a liquidation-based claim on cheapness, and it is only meaningful if those current assets are actually realizable — so the accrual-verification requirement is far more binding for a liquidation anchor than for a going-concern book anchor, where earning power rather than asset realizability drives the discount.
evaluated.reasoning: Unlike the rejected multi-anchor proposal, this is not motivated by measurement error in cheapness but by a different economic claim: the liquidation anchor is built from the very current-asset accounts whose quality the verification leg tests, so the interaction is intrinsic rather than incidental and should be strictly stronger here than under book-to-market. Subtracting long-term debt keeps the anchor a genuine residual claim, and all inputs have coverage comparable to the leading signals.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: EqualWeightSelfFundedValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ADD(IND_RANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1))), ADD(IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), MA(sale, 3)), 1))), IND_RANK(WINSOR(GROWTH(sale, 1), 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Share retirement, working-capital release, and revenue growth are three co-equal signatures of internally financed, cash-collected operations, and the value premium among cheap firms should be graded by how many of these signatures are present rather than dominated by any one of them.
evaluated.reasoning: This repairs a concrete defect the critic identified in the archive's multi-leg composites: nested SUMRANK silently gives the outer leg twice the weight of each inner leg, so every three-channel signal tested so far has been a disguised two-thirds bet on share issuance. Summing three separately computed industry ranks enforces genuinely equal weighting, which is a structural correction with a testable prediction — if the equal-weighted version beats SelfFundedGrowthValue, the archive's earlier three-leg results understated the operating channels.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: SharpTrapFreeVerifiedValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), NEG(MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), MA(sale, 3)), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(GROWTH(sale, 1), 1))))))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Trap avoidance should be graded continuously by how jointly severe the two warning signs are, not by whichever is milder: multiplying the accrual-buildup percentile by the demand-decline percentile produces a red-flag intensity that is near zero unless both conditions hold.
evaluated.reasoning: The critic correctly noted that NEG(MIN(a,b)) is a permissive "either flag absent" screen that discards much of the conjunctive information, so this replaces it with the strict product while holding the gate, the financing leg, the deflators and the aggregation identical. Given that the permissive version already delivered the archive's largest reliable alpha, sharpening the conjunction is the highest-value single-parameter refinement available in the final round.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: DualHabitVerifiedValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(NEG(DELTA(csho, 1)), 0), 3), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(NEG(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), 0), 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What verifies a cheap firm's accounting is habit rather than magnitude on both sides of the ledger: how many of the last three years it retired shares, and how many it released working capital, with magnitudes discarded because they are dominated by one-off tenders, acquisitions and writedowns.
evaluated.reasoning: Converting the accrual leg to a persistence count preserved alpha and produced a strong FMB slope (t = 3.43, fmb 4.84), so the untested question is whether the financing leg benefits from the same coarsening — magnitudes of share-count change are notoriously contaminated by option exercise and equity-financed acquisitions. Two four-valued legs also produce a very stable portfolio composition, which should raise Sharpe and cut turnover if the effect is genuinely behavioural.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: JointDisciplineYears
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(TS_SUM(MUL(INDICATOR(NEG(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), 0), INDICATOR(NEG(DELTA(csho, 1)), 0)), 3)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The strongest evidence that reported profits are collected is the number of years in which a firm simultaneously released working capital and retired shares — cash freed from the operating cycle in the same year it was handed to shareholders — because contemporaneous co-occurrence rules out the possibility that one channel was funded by the other or by borrowing.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a single conjunctive state variable rather than a rank-sum of two channels, so it tests whether verification is about co-occurrence within the year or merely about both properties being present on average — a distinction no archived signal can resolve. It is also maximally parsimonious, with one bounded 0-to-3 quality score inside the proven gate-and-standardize architecture.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: IssuanceFundedStaleAccrualTrap
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), MA(sale, 3)), 1)), MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(GROWTH(sale, 1), 1))), IND_RANK(WINSOR(GROWTH(csho, 1), 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The archetypal value trap is a cheap firm that is building receivables and inventories while revenue falls and is issuing equity to pay for it: uncollected profits, deteriorating demand and external funding of the shortfall together predict severe underperformance.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a strict triple conjunction rather than the sign-flipped mirror of the long-side composite — a firm needs high percentiles on all three flags to score highly, so the informative short leg is a homogeneous group rather than a linear combination of the same channels reversed. It provides the final batch with sign-symmetric evidence for the mechanism, using the same primitives whose long-side conjunction produced the archive's largest reliable alpha.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ChronicTrapVerifiedValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), NEG(TS_SUM(MUL(INDICATOR(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), 0), INDICATOR(NEG(GROWTH(sale, 1)), 0)), 3)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A single year of accrual buildup during a demand decline can be a cyclical accident, but a firm that has been in that state repeatedly over three years is chronically failing to convert reported sales into cash; the count of trap-years, not its current severity, is what separates a temporarily depressed cheap stock from a deteriorating one.
evaluated.reasoning: This is not a recombination of the two frontier legs but a new statistic applied to the trap state itself — chronicity rather than either current intensity (TrapFreeVerifiedValue) or the frequency of the benign state (PersistentReleaseVerifiedValue) — so a positive result identifies persistence of the *pathology* as the operative concept and a null cleanly rules it out. Because the count is discrete and slow-moving, it should produce a stable low-turnover portfolio while the retirement leg supplies the continuous cash-return dimension.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: WorkingCapitalFlexibilityValue
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(WINSOR(ADD(TS_MAX(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), MA(sale, 3)), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), MA(sale, 3)), 5)), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What protects a cheap firm is the ability to turn accrual assets back into cash when needed: if over five years its largest working-capital release exceeds its largest buildup, the operating cycle is flexible and the receivables and inventories on its balance sheet are genuinely realizable, whereas a firm that builds sharply and never releases holds claims it cannot monetize.
evaluated.reasoning: Summing the five-year maximum and minimum of the working-capital flow measures the *asymmetry* of the accrual distribution — a third-moment concept that the archive has never tested, distinct from the level, change, persistence count, and volatility formulations, and economically distinct because it speaks to realizability under stress rather than to average discipline. It also replaces the failed volatility experiment with the right sign logic: instability per se was not informative, but release-skewed instability should be, and unlike the earlier attempt the flow is sales-deflated and winsorized so cash-heavy firms cannot drive the extremes.
evaluated.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualPurgedBookValueYield
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(ceq, TS_SUM(SUB(ib, oancf), 3)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
considered.hypothesis: Book equity built up by three years of cumulative accruals is soft capital that will be reversed or written off; removing cumulative accruals from the numerator yields a "cash-verified" book value whose ratio to market price is a cleaner measure of true cheapness.
considered.reasoning: This restates the valuation ratio itself rather than combining two scores, so accruals enter as a balance-sheet correction to the value anchor. Firms with high purged book-to-market are cheap on assets that have been validated by cash generation, and should outperform nominally cheap firms whose equity is accrual residue.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: PersistentCashBackingEarningsYield
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(SUB(oancf, ib), 0), 5))
considered.hypothesis: A single year of clean accruals can be noise; a five-year count of years in which operating cash flow exceeded reported income measures durable conservatism, and high earnings yield combined with persistent cash backing identifies genuinely mispriced firms rather than temporarily flattered ones.
considered.reasoning: The indicator-sum converts accrual quality into a persistence state, filtering out firms whose good accrual year is transitory. Pairing this with earnings-to-price makes the value signal credible only when the earnings stream has repeatedly been validated by cash.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashVersusEarningsValueGap
considered.expression: SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))))
considered.hypothesis: Investors anchor valuation on reported earnings rather than cash flow, so firms that rank cheap on operating-cash-flow yield but only mediocre on earnings yield are systematically underpriced; the divergence between the two valuation rankings, measured within industry, is the mispricing rather than either level.
considered.reasoning: Instead of adding a value score to an accrual score, this measures the same firm's position in two competing valuation ladders whose only difference is the accrual component of income, so the signal is zero by construction when earnings are fully cash-backed. Industry ranking removes sector-level differences in normal accrual intensity and in typical multiples, isolating firms whose price reflects accrual-laden earnings instead of the cash they actually generate.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualGradedValue
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at))))
considered.hypothesis: The value premium scales continuously with accounting conservatism: book-to-market should be discounted in proportion to how accrual-dependent reported income is, so weighting cheapness by the firm's percentile of accrual conservatism produces a monotone "credible value" signal.
considered.reasoning: Replacing the hard indicator with a [0,1] cross-sectional percentile removes the mass point at zero, so the low-signal bucket is populated by genuinely expensive or accrual-inflated firms rather than a mixture of gated names. Winsorizing book-to-market keeps distressed and near-zero-price observations from dominating the product while preserving full coverage of the value dimension.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CheapAtCashConversionPeak
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1), TS_RANK(RATIO(oancf, ebitda), 5))
considered.hypothesis: Cash conversion of pre-accrual profitability (oancf divided by ebitda) is an unambiguous accrual-quality state: when a cheap firm sits near the top of its own five-year cash-conversion history, its depressed multiple reflects stale accrual skepticism that is being resolved by realized cash.
considered.reasoning: Using ebitda as the denominator fixes the sign ambiguity the critic raised, since a rising ratio cannot be produced by falling income the way a falling (ib − oancf)/at can. The self-referenced TS_RANK converts accrual quality into a firm-specific state variable and gates the EBITDA-to-price cheapness signal, so the interaction is dynamic and conditional rather than an additive rank sum.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: GlamourAccrualOverstatement
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), IND_RANK(RATIO(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ceq)))
considered.hypothesis: Accrual mispricing is concentrated where expectations are extrapolated: highly valued (low book-to-market) firms that report income unsupported by operating cash flow face the largest subsequent earnings disappointment and negative returns, while the same accruals in cheap firms are already priced.
considered.reasoning: This reverses the earlier premise to match the documented concentration of the accrual anomaly in glamour stocks, using an industry-ranked price-to-book gate in [0,1] that amplifies accruals for expensive firms and shrinks them toward zero for value firms. The high-signal (short) leg is therefore unambiguously accrual-heavy glamour, and the low-signal (long) leg is cash-generating glamour plus neutral value names, giving an interpretable spread with a clean negative expected sign.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashSalesToPrice
considered.expression: RATIO(ADD(sale, ADD(recch, invch)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
considered.hypothesis: Sales-to-price is a strong value signal only when revenue converts into cash; adjusting sales for receivable and inventory build-ups (cash-flow-statement decrease items, negative when working capital expands) yields a cash sales yield that avoids revenue-recognition-driven value traps.
considered.reasoning: Operating-cycle accruals are the specific accrual channel that contaminates revenue-based valuation, so correcting the numerator of the sales multiple targets the mechanism directly rather than adding a generic accrual score. It tests a different valuation anchor (revenue) and a different accrual primitive (working-capital cash-flow items) than Signals 1–3.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: OpaqueValueAccrualInstability
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Cheapness is only investable when the accounting is legible: firms with volatile, unstable accruals are informationally opaque, so their low multiples reflect justified uncertainty, while cheap firms with stable accrual behavior are genuinely mispriced.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the level of accruals with the second moment of accruals, a distinct information-risk mechanism rather than an earnings-overstatement mechanism, gated onto an EBITDA-based cheapness measure that is itself pre-accrual. If it outperforms Signal 1, the interaction is about accounting reliability rather than accrual direction.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ConjunctiveValueAccrualScreen
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at))))
considered.hypothesis: Cheapness and accrual conservatism are complements, not substitutes: the value premium is earned only when a firm passes both screens, so the expected return is governed by the weaker of the two percentile scores rather than by their average.
considered.reasoning: Working in bounded industry-rank space removes the negative-book-equity perversity of the multiplicative gate, since a good accrual rank can no longer push a distressed firm further into the short leg. The MIN aggregation is a substantively different claim from the published additive value-plus-accruals composite: it predicts no premium for accrual-clean expensive firms or for accrual-heavy cheap firms, which a linear blend rewards partially.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualRegimeReversalValue
considered.expression: SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Cheap firms whose current accruals sit at the low end of their own five-year accrual history have already absorbed the reversal of past aggressive reporting; the market extrapolates the recent weak reported earnings, so the discount is stale and mean-reverts upward.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the flawed "purged equity" arithmetic entirely, so no depreciation add-back can inflate the valuation anchor: depreciation enters only inside a self-referenced time-series rank, where firm-level capital intensity is differenced away. The mechanism is a within-firm accrual regime state (reversal completed) interacted with cross-sectional cheapness, which is distinct from any accrual-level composite.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: HardBookToMarket
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(ceq, SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
considered.hypothesis: Book equity composed of receivables, inventories and other soft operating working capital is far less reliable collateral for a value claim than equity composed of cash and long-lived assets; restating the value anchor on hard, non-accrual equity identifies cheapness that is not an artifact of accrual-inflated current assets.
considered.reasoning: This is not operating cash flow to price, because it uses the stock of net operating working capital rather than its change, so it cannot collapse to the documented CF/P anomaly and it prices the accumulated accrual balance that reversal risk actually lives on. Firms whose book equity is mostly working capital receive a sharply lower signal even at identical B/M, which is exactly the value-trap distinction the theme calls for.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: OpaqueOtherAccrualValue
considered.expression: SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(ABS(RATIO(aoloch, at))))
considered.hypothesis: Large "other" operating asset and liability adjustments are the least verifiable accrual component and proxy for accounting opacity; cheapness is credible when the cash-flow reconciliation is dominated by transparent items, and is a trap when a big unexplained residual accrual drives reported operations.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the published glamour-conditioned accrual result with an untested opacity channel on the value side, and taking absolute magnitude makes the quality leg sign-unambiguous (both large positive and large negative residual accruals indicate unverifiable reporting). Because both legs are industry ranks, the long leg is cheap-and-transparent and the short leg is expensive-and-opaque, avoiding the perverse mixed long leg of the earlier multiplicative form.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashEbitdaToEnterpriseValue
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(ebitda, DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)))
considered.hypothesis: Operating profit that must be reinvested in receivables and inventories is not distributable to capital providers; measuring cheapness as working-capital-adjusted EBITDA per dollar of enterprise value identifies firms whose whole-capital-structure multiple is supported by cash-convertible profit rather than by working-capital-inflated accounting profit.
considered.reasoning: The enterprise-value denominator prices debt and net cash, making this a different valuation anchor from book-to-market and hence less collinear with HML, while the numerator subtracts the exact accrual component that makes EBITDA unreliable. It tests whether moving the interaction into an EV multiple recovers the FF5 alpha that equity-only value anchors failed to deliver.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SoftCapitalBackedPriceTrap
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
considered.hypothesis: What matters for a value trap is not the annual accrual flow but the accumulated stock of soft operating capital standing behind the price: when a large share of market value is claimed by receivables and inventories net of operating liabilities, the equity claim rests on assets whose realization is uncertain and whose write-down is pending, so such firms underperform.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the flow-over-market-cap deflator (a known accrual-anomaly robustness variant) with the balance-sheet accrual *stock* per dollar of price, a quantity that is not the accrual anomaly variable and that decomposes book-to-market into its hard and soft halves. Paired with the archived HardBookToMarket it delivers a clean decomposition test: if the hard half carries the positive slope and the soft half a negative one, the value premium is genuinely accrual-quality conditional rather than uniform.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CheapnessWeightedAccrualQuality
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Accrual conservatism is priced only where the market has already assigned a low multiple, so the correct signal is accrual quality amplified by the firm's cheapness percentile: among expensive firms the accrual term is muted, among cheap firms it fully separates cash-backed value from accrual-supported value traps.
considered.reasoning: Unlike the symmetric z-score product, one leg is a bounded [0,1] cheapness weight and only the accrual leg is signed, so the long and short extremes are both drawn from cheap firms (clean versus dirty) instead of pooling cheap-clean with expensive-dirty. That construction also makes the spread approximately value-neutral, which directly targets the gen-1 failure in which static-value loadings caused FF5 to absorb or over-price the entire raw spread.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashFundedExpansionValue
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUB(RATIO(DELTA(che, 1), at), RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at))))
considered.hypothesis: For a cheap firm the informative question is what its balance sheet grew into: cash accumulation means reported profits were collected, while growth concentrated in receivables and inventories means profits exist only on paper, so the cash-versus-soft-capital composition of expansion discriminates real from illusory cheapness.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the flawed price-driven "value news" leg — which was mechanically past return and thus a reversal bet — with a purely fundamental composition measure that contains no price change at all. Because the cheapness term enters as a bounded weight, the long-short spread again compares cheap firms with cheap firms, so the mechanism is testable without an embedded HML position.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CurrentLiabilityStretchedValue
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(DELTA(lct, 1), MA(sale, 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Cheap firms that expand payables and accrued liabilities faster than their normalized revenue are financing operations by stretching suppliers and deferring recognized costs, which simultaneously flatters operating cash flow and raises refinancing risk, so their low multiple reflects a deteriorating rather than a temporarily depressed business.
considered.reasoning: This tests the liability side of the accrual construct, a channel none of the archived signals touches, and normalizing by three-year average sales avoids the scale artifacts of asset deflation for firms with shrinking balance sheets. Because it explicitly predicts a negative slope within the cheap cohort, it also serves as the sign-symmetric counterpart to Signal 2: both should be strong if the trap mechanism is real, and their disagreement would localize whether asset-side or liability-side accruals drive the effect.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: WorstFlawPenalizedValue
considered.expression: SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MAX(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at), 1)), IND_RANK(ABS(RATIO(aoloch, at)))))
considered.hypothesis: Accounting credibility is destroyed by whichever red flag is worst, not by their average: a cheap firm is a trap if either its working-capital accruals are large or its cash-flow reconciliation is dominated by unexplained other-accrual items, so cheapness should be penalized by the maximum of the two flaw percentiles.
considered.reasoning: The MAX operates on the accrual side rather than across themes, which is a different aggregation claim from the archived MIN screen: it lets two economically distinct accounting flaws substitute for each other as disqualifiers while keeping a single continuous value ladder. Winsorizing the accrual leg and using absolute opacity keeps both flaw measures sign-unambiguous and bounded, and comparing this to the archived single-flaw versions tells us whether accrual red flags are additive or worst-case in their pricing effect.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashShareOfCurrentAssetsValue
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(che, act)))
considered.hypothesis: The stock analogue of the winning flow signal: among cheap firms, those whose current assets are held as cash rather than as receivables and inventories have already collected their reported profits, whereas cheap firms whose liquidity is locked in soft claims face reversal and write-down risk.
considered.reasoning: CashFundedExpansionValue showed that the cash-versus-soft-capital composition of the balance sheet, weighted by cheapness, produces FF5 alpha; this tests whether the effect lives in the level of composition or only in its annual change, which is the single most useful thing to learn about that mechanism. The ratio is bounded in [0,1] by construction, so the accrual leg needs no winsorization and the long-short legs are both drawn from cheap firms, keeping the spread near value-neutral.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SoftCapitalPerEnterpriseValue
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)))
considered.hypothesis: The value trap is that total invested capital, not just equity, is committed to soft operating claims: when receivables and inventories net of operating liabilities consume a large share of enterprise value, both shareholders and creditors are exposed to accrual reversal, and expected returns are lower than the firm's factor loadings imply.
considered.reasoning: This isolates the deflator choice in the archive's strongest portfolio result, replacing market equity with enterprise value so that the signal is no longer mechanically inflated by leverage and thin equity capitalization. If the negative alpha survives the debt-inclusive deflator, the trap is about the composition of invested capital rather than about a levered small-cap value tilt.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: WorkingCapitalTurnoverValue
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(sale, SUB(act, che))))
considered.hypothesis: Accrual assets are only dangerous when they are unproductive: a cheap firm that turns each dollar of receivables and inventory into many dollars of revenue is converting accruals into realized sales quickly, while a cheap firm with slow working-capital turnover is warehousing claims that will be written down.
considered.reasoning: This introduces a new channel — the velocity of accrual assets rather than their level, change, or composition — while keeping the cheapness-weight structure that produced the archive's only positive alpha. Turnover is a strictly positive, well-scaled quantity with broad coverage, and industry z-scoring removes the large sector differences in normal operating-cycle length.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: WorkedDownWorkingCapitalValue
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), at), 5), RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), at))))
considered.hypothesis: A cheap firm that has already worked its receivable and inventory bloat well below its own five-year peak has completed the accrual reversal the market feared, so its discount is stale; a cheap firm still sitting at its historical working-capital peak has the reversal, and the associated write-downs, still ahead of it.
considered.reasoning: This is a distance-from-own-extreme state rather than a level, a one-year change, or a cumulative flow, so it is not a horizon reparameterization of CashFundedExpansionValue: two firms with identical current accruals and identical annual changes receive opposite scores depending on where they stand relative to their own historical bloat. Keeping the cheapness term as a bounded weight preserves the near value-neutral long-short structure that produced the archive's only positive alpha, while the five-year window supplies the reversal-completion concept the mechanism requires.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: DebtFinancedSoftCapitalTrap
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), MA(at, 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Soft operating capital is most dangerous when it is financed by creditors rather than by equity: a levered firm whose market value is largely backed by receivables and inventories faces creditor-forced liquidation of exactly those claims at distressed prices, so the combination of high soft-capital-per-price and high leverage predicts returns below factor loadings.
